crossrefs.text: These things serve as illustrations, for the women represent two covenants. One covenant is from Mount Sinai and bears children into slavery: This is Hagar.
He treated Abram well on her account, and Abram acquired sheep and cattle, male and female donkeys, menservants and maidservants, and camels.
But Abram replied, “O Lord God, what can You give me, since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?”
Abram continued, “Behold, You have given me no offspring, so a servant in my household will be my heir.”
But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son,
and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave womanʼs son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!”
May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field that the LordGod had made. And he said to the woman, “Did God really say, ‘You must not eat from any tree in the garden?’” The woman answered the serpent, “We may eat the fruit of the trees of the garden, but about the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, ‘You must not eat of it or touch it, or you will die.’” “You will not surely die,” the serpent told the woman. “For God knows that in the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

notes.title: Hagar and Sarah as two covenants

crossrefs.text: O LORD, You have searched me and known me.
even the darkness is not dark to You, but the night shines like the day, for darkness is as light to You.
So Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.”
For a manʼs ways are before the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD examines all his paths.
After a long time, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned and cried out under their burden of slavery, and their cry for deliverance from bondage ascended to God.
So God heard their groaning, and He remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.
The LORD said, “I have indeed seen the affliction of My people in Egypt. I have heard them crying out because of their oppressors, and I am aware of their sufferings.

Ishmael: twelve princes and a great nation

crossrefs.text: The angel of the Lordproceeded: “Behold, you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the Lordhas heard your cry of affliction.
And Abraham said to God, “O that Ishmael might live under Your blessing!”
As for Ishmael, I have heard you, and I will surely bless him; I will make him fruitful and multiply him greatly. He will become the father of twelve rulers, and I will make him into a great nation.
and his son Ishmael was thirteen; Abraham and his son Ishmael were circumcised on the same day.

But Sarah saw that the son whom Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son, and she said to Abraham, “Expel the slave woman and her son, for the slave womanʼs son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!” Now this matter distressed Abraham greatly because it concerned his son Ishmael. But God said to Abraham, “Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant. Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned. But I will also make a nation of the slave womanʼs son, because he is your offspring.”
His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.
This is the account of Abrahamʼs son Ishmael, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarahʼs maidservant, bore to Abraham.
Esau went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Abrahamʼs son Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had.
